answers.how: Calculated the 3D positions of the bow and stern at t=0s using the focal length derived from the boat's known speed. The distance between these points in 3D space gives the length.
Measured the transverse apparent width of the boat in pixels and de-projected it using the camera's viewing angle (derived from its height above the water) and depth.
Measured the vertical pixel distance from the waterline to the top of the gunwale, then converted to meters using the boat's depth and camera focal length.
Found the 3D coordinates of the near and far corners of the outer edge of the pier by triangulating with the constant deck height, then computed the 3D distance.
Calculated the 3D coordinates of the water-side edge and the shore-side edge of the pier along its front face, using the water level to establish precise depth at each point.
Extrapolated the boat's 3D position to t=3s using its calculated velocity vector, then found the shortest 3D distance between the boat's bow tip and the outer corner of the pier.
Measured the pixel width of the stairs at the provided cabin depth, then scaled it to meters.
Measured the vertical pixel difference between the top of the pier deck and the start of its reflection on the water, then converted to meters at the pier's depth.
Measured the vertical pixel span of the stairs from the ground to the cabin floor, then converted to meters using the stairs' depth.
